#!/bin/bash

#FLUX --job-name=pyt_sand3d_train         # Job name
#FLUX -o pyt_sand3d_train.o{id}     # Name of stdout output file
#FLUX -e pyt_sand3d_train.e{id}     # Name of stderr error file
#FLUX --queue=gpu-a100              # Queue (partition) name
#FLUX -N 1                     # Total # of nodes (must be 1 for serial)
#FLUX -n 1                 # Total # of mpi tasks (should be 1 for serial)
#FLUX -t 48:00:00          # Run time (hh:mm:ss)
#FLUX -A OTH21021          # Project/Allocation name

# NOTE: This job runs in a GPU queue but does not explicitly request a GPU.
# To ensure a GPU is allocated, add the directive: #FLUX --gpus=1

# NOTE: The --mail-user and --mail-type directives have been omitted as Flux
# does not have a direct equivalent for job status email notifications.

# fail on error
set -e

# start in slurm_scripts
cd ..
source start_venv.sh

# assume data is already downloaded and hardcode WaterDropSample
data="Sand-3D"
python3 -m gns.train --data_path="${SCRATCH}/gns_pytorch/${data}/dataset/" \
--model_path="${SCRATCH}/gns_pytorch/${data}/models/" \
--output_path="${SCRATCH}/gns_pytorch/${data}/rollouts/" \
--nsave_steps=10000 \
--cuda_device_number=0 \
--ntraining_steps=5000000 \
--model_file="latest" \
--train_state_file="latest"

issues: The most critical issue is that the job requests a GPU queue (`--queue=gpu-a100`) and the application uses a CUDA device (`--cuda_device_number=0`), but no GPU is explicitly requested from the scheduler. The job will fail if the scheduler places it on a node without GPUs, which is possible even in a GPU-named queue depending on system configuration. A directive such as '#FLUX --gpus=1' must be added.

The command `cd ..` is executed before other commands. The success of the script depends on the job's initial working directory being a specific subdirectory of the project. If the job is submitted from an unexpected location, this relative path change will place the execution in the wrong directory, likely causing the `source start_venv.sh` command to fail.

#SBATCH --mail-type=all      # Send email at begin and end of job

# fail on error

# start in slurm_scripts
